description: A five-block sequencer where the next block is chosen by a grid of transition chances rather than by counting in order

params.text: One beat of the sequence, holding up to four notes in one of nine subdivisions; left click to step forward, shift and left click to step back, right click to choose from a list
Sets the pitch of one note in the block: click for a keyboard carrying Rest, Tie and an Auto Advance button, or drag up and down to set the voltage
Sets the chance of moving from one note block to another: click to switch that move on or off, drag up and down to set its probability, and hover over it to show which move it is

inputs.text: Advances the sequence one note block
Returns the sequence to its first note block when the voltage rises past 2V

outputs.text: High while a note is playing, for the length set on the menu
The pitch of the note now playing
A gate at the end of each cycle

notes: nothing happens until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
a block with no outgoing transition switched on has nowhere to go, so set at least one chance in each block's row before playing
this build has five note blocks and a five by five transition grid; the maker's manual says eight blocks
the five squares on the diagonal of the grid would be a block moving to itself; they carry no button and cannot be clicked
menu: Transition Mode: Chance, Cycle — Chance picks one switched-on move at random, each weight being its probability; Cycle takes them in a fixed order, the weights setting how often each comes up
Arrow Display Mode: On, Only Hover, Off — chooses when the arrow overlays are drawn: from the current block unless the cursor is over a transition, only under the cursor, or never
Gate Length — sets how much of each note the gate output stays high for
Swing — delays every second note block
Clock Mode: Gate, Phase — reads the clock input either as a square wave, high above 2V and low below 0.1V, or as a ramp that advances a block when it falls from above 9V to below 1V
Randomize — randomises the pitches, the rhythm or the transition grid
Shift & Shuffle — shifts and shuffles the sequence from the menu, the way the Shift & Shuffle expander does from its jacks
Set Rhythm — sets every note block to one subdivision
Note Pool — sets the pool of notes the randomisers draw from, from a scale, from a keyboard, or by shifting the current pool in semitones
Copy/Paste — copies and pastes the sequence or the note pool in a portable format that other JP sequencers read
Expanders — places an expander module beside this one
